title: Wringer bench event
description: ONE LINE of `bench.jsonl`, not the file. Append-only, one JSON object per line, every line carrying `prev_hash` — the sha256 of the line before it, or 64 zeros for the first — verified by the same chain function `wring audit` uses, not a lookalike. Every string value is scrubbed by the redactor before it is written. Absence is meaningful throughout: a key appears only in the case it describes, and NO key here orders contenders (SPEC_BENCH_V0 ruling 6 — bench measures and does not crown).

ts.description: Local ISO-8601 with offset, millisecond precision — fine enough to order two fast events, coarse enough to stay readable.

prev_hash.description: sha256 of the previous line, or 64 zeros for the first. Makes the LEDGER tamper-evident and says nothing about the rest of the bundle — that is `digests.json`'s job.

oneOf.title: bench.started
oneOf.description: The conditions every row below was measured under, recorded before any of them ran.

sha.description: The baseline worktree's detached HEAD. Every contender worktree was checked against this one and a disagreement was refused, so one sha describes the whole bench.

contenders.description: The selected contender ids, in DECLARED order. An array of ids here; `bench.finished` records a count under its own name, because one field meaning two things across two events is how a format becomes unreadable after it is frozen.

contender_wall_clock.description: The SAME ceiling handed to every contender's loop — never a remainder, so no contender is measured under conditions its predecessor set.

oneOf.title: baseline.verified
oneOf.description: The statement of the job. A bench needs something to repair, so a baseline where no required gate fails is refused (exit 1) and writes no bundle at all — which is why this event only ever records a failing status.

failing_gates.description: The required gates that failed at the baseline: the work every contender was measured on.

run_ref.description: The baseline's verify bundle, by path, never nested — inside the kept baseline worktree.

oneOf.title: contender.finished
oneOf.description: One contender's result. Two kinds of number with different authority: everything except `usage` is Wringer's own measurement, and `usage` is the AGENT'S OWN CLAIM, recorded verbatim and unverified. A contender that failed to converge is a RESULT here, not a bench failure.

outcome.description: A loop reason, or `error` when the loop raised rather than returned. Not a grade: `no_progress` is a measurement, and nothing ranks it against `converged`.

loop_ref.description: The contender's loop bundle, by path, inside its kept worktree. Never nested: one run, one bundle, one place.

head_moved.description: Whether the worker moved its worktree's HEAD. The harness never writes git history, but a worker is somebody else's agent and may commit — and every tree-anchored verdict in this row is then relative to a tree the agent moved.

final_run.description: The VERIFY bundle the loop's last verification wrote, rebased onto the repo root — the path `wring judge` can actually be handed. Absent when the loop verified nothing.

agent.description: Present only when the contender was declared as `agent:` sugar: the table id the author wrote. The COMMAND behind it stays in `agents.py`, where every vendor string lives.

usage.description: PRESENT ONLY when the agent reported it. Absent means unreported, NEVER zero — a zero here would be a number Wringer made up about somebody else's spending. There is no price table: cost is what the agent said it was, in the agent's own currency, or it is absent.

cost.description: Present only when every reporting row shared one currency. Mixed currencies produce no total, because adding them would need an exchange rate — a live vendor fact with a shelf life, which this program deliberately does not hold.

oneOf.title: bench.finished
oneOf.description: An interrupted bench still writes its manifest and digests over what exists, so a bundle without this line is a partial bench somebody may still audit — not a broken one.

rows.description: How many contender rows were written. A COUNT, under its own name — `bench.started`'s `contenders` is an array of ids, and reusing that key for a number would freeze an ambiguity into a published format.
